analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/developer/test.md, which is documentation only. I saw no code, configuration, secret, or runtime-behavior change in them, and no patch hunks were supplied. Only head text was provided, so I could not tell which lines are newly added versus pre-existing.

Security-relevant content in the excerpts:
- Cache-scope and SSD tests are described (lines ~1317-1350, 1421-1437) that cover T-041, SEC-035 and A-001. They state that fixtures do not qualify multi-host routing, signed key durability or hosted account trust, and that ephemeral cache keys are not production attestation. These statements are consistent with the T-041 posture and do not overclaim.
- Lines 1385-1419 reference App Attest worker tests and native qualification. They say that signing is not Apple acceptance, that opt-in native failures must not become skips, and that transport fixtures are not serving qualification. This matches TB-011, T-052 and T-057, and does not weaken the stated qualification boundaries.
- Lines 1692-1715 and 1837-1839 require disposable DATABASE_URL databases and warn against pointing tests at shared or production databases. The documentation retains this isolation guidance; it does not weaken it.
- Lines 1760 and 1791 describe sanitized environments and fixture-only transports that reject redirects and proxies.
- Lines 1951-1963 state that synthetic provider output does not establish cache hits or model quality.

No asset, trust boundary, assumption or mitigation is invalidated. I see no need to update the threat model for these excerpts. For the next pass: anything beyond these docs lines, such as code changes behind the described tests, was not in this batch. The two units are mid-file excerpts, so other parts of the same file and other PR files are not covered by this analysis.
